title: Emergency medicine and critical care
audience: a medical student in the clinical years preparing for the USMLE
purpose: Approach the undifferentiated patient, run resuscitations, manage shock and sepsis, chest pain, dyspnea, abdominal pain, trauma, poisoning and environmental emergencies, airway and ventilation, critical care drugs and monitoring, neurological emergencies, and disposition and handoffs.

weeks.4: Chest pain and dyspnea in the emergency department
weeks.5: Abdominal pain in the emergency department
weeks.10: Critical care: vasopressors, sedation and monitoring

blocks.deliverable: Run a cardiac arrest algorithm step by step.
Classify shock from supplied vital signs and examination.
Identify the can't-miss causes of abdominal pain.
Week 7 midterm; recognize toxidromes and give the antidotes.
Choose a vasopressor for each type of shock.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Resuscitation scenarios: work through three supplied simulation cases step by step, then write the critical actions and a debrief for each.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
